第 6 章　廠商的擁有權Chapter 6　Ownership of firms

對齊新版 UPEP《活用經濟學 1》第 6 章（6.1–6.3）。本章專教私有制下的獨資、合夥、私人有限公司和公眾有限公司，股票和債券，以及公有制下的政府部門和公營公司。 Aligned with UPEP Economics in Action 1 Chapter 6 (sections 6.1–6.3). This chapter is private ownership (sole proprietorships, partnerships, private limited companies and public limited companies), shares and bonds, and public ownership (government departments and public corporations).

6.1A 6.1B 6.2 6.3 詞彙Terms

學習重點Learning focus

讀完本章，應能：

After this chapter you should be able to:

6.1A 東主承擔無限債務責任的私營企業Private enterprises whose owners bear unlimited liability

廠商是生產單位，它就僱用生產要素以及生產物品與服務作出決策。廠商不一定有一個實體地點。廠商的商業擁有權可大致分為：

A firm is a production unit. It makes decisions about the employment of factors of production and the production of goods and services. It may not have a physical location. The business ownership of firms can be broadly divided into:

  • 公有制（由政府擁有）；及public ownership (owned by the government); and
  • 私有制（由私人擁有）。private ownership (owned by private individuals).

私有制下經營的廠商稱為私營企業，由私人擁有。

Firms under private ownership are called private enterprises. They are owned by private individuals.

根據東主所承擔的債務責任，私營企業可分為以下兩類：

According to the liability borne by their owners, private enterprises can be classified into two types:

  1. 東主承擔無限債務責任的私營企業Private enterprises whose owners bear unlimited liability
  2. 東主承擔有限債務責任的私營企業（稱為有限公司）Private enterprises whose owners bear limited liability (limited companies)

無限債務責任是指東主的債務責任不限於其投資在廠商的金額。

Unlimited liability means that owners’ liability is not confined to the amount of their investment in the firm.

有限債務責任是指東主的債務責任僅限於其投資在廠商的金額。

Limited liability means that owners’ liability is confined to the amount of their investment in the firm.

上述兩類私營企業可進一步細分如下（圖 6.1）：

The two forms of private enterprises can be further classified as follows (Fig. 6.1):

圖 6.1　私營企業的分類Fig. 6.1 Classification of private enterprises

獨資和合夥Sole proprietorships and partnerships

東主承擔無限債務責任的私營企業分為以下兩種：獨資和合夥。

There are two types of private enterprises whose owners bear unlimited liability: sole proprietorships and partnerships.

獨資只有一名東主，該東主承擔無限債務責任。

A sole proprietorship has only one owner who bears unlimited liability.

獨資的東主稱為獨資經營者，他為其廠商承擔所有責任，同時亦享有廠商的所有利潤。

The owner is called a sole proprietor. He bears all responsibilities of the firm. In return, he enjoys all the profits from it.

合夥擁有兩名或以上的東主，這些東主承擔無限債務責任。

A partnership has two or more owners who bear unlimited liability.

合夥的東主稱為合夥人。他們通常會簽訂合夥協議，概述各合夥人的權利和責任。

The owners are called partners. They usually have a partnership agreement outlining the rights and responsibilities of the partners.

在本章，「合夥」一詞是指普通合夥。普通合夥的所有合夥人都要承擔無限債務責任。其他的合夥形式不包括在課程之內。

The term ‘partnership’ in this chapter refers to general partnership. All partners in a general partnership have unlimited liability. Other types of partnerships are NOT required in the syllabus.

① 獨資和合夥的共同特徵① Common features of sole proprietorships and partnerships

a. 不是法人

a. Not a legal entity

獨資和合夥並不是法人。

Sole proprietorships and partnerships are not legal entities.

東主須承擔企業的所有法律責任。這意味着東主以個人名義（而非廠商名義）擁有財產、簽訂合同和參與訴訟。

The owners need to personally bear all legal responsibilities for the firms. This means that owners (not the firms) are the ones who own properties, make contracts and engage in lawsuits.

課本 p.4

Textbook p. 4

圖 6.2　獨資經營者須為其廠商負上法律責任。Fig. 6.2 A sole proprietor has legal responsibilities for the firm.

參與訴訟包括起訴別人和被人起訴。

Engaging in lawsuits includes suing others and being sued.

b. 無限債務責任

b. Unlimited liability

東主承擔無限債務責任，即他們的債務責任不限於其投資在廠商的金額。

Owners bear unlimited liability, i.e., their liability is not limited to the amount of their investment in the firm.

獨資經營者和合夥人均要對其廠商的債務負上全部責任。他們可能要以個人資產來償還廠商的債務。

Both sole proprietors and partners are fully responsible for the debts of their firms. They may have to use their personal assets to settle their firms’ debts.

課本 p.5

Textbook p. 5

圖 6.3　獨資經營者和合夥人可能要出售個人財產，如汽車、名貴手錶和物業，以償還其廠商的債務。Fig. 6.3 Sole proprietors and partners may need to sell their own assets, such as cars, luxury watches and houses, to repay the debts of their firms.

c. 缺乏延續性

c. Lack of continuity

獨資和合夥均不是法人。當任何一名東主破產、死亡或退出業務時，該廠商就要解散。因此，這些廠商缺乏延續性。

Sole proprietorships and partnerships are not legal entities. The firms will be dissolved when any of the owners goes bankrupt, dies or withdraws from the business. Therefore, the firms have no lasting continuity.

課本 p.5　愛美、明德和建宏以合夥方式經營一家麵包店。如果建宏退出業務，原有的合夥便會解散。若要繼續營運，愛美和明德要成立新的合夥。

Textbook p. 5　Amy, Bill and Carl run a bakery as a partnership. If Carl withdraws from the business, the original partnership will be dissolved. To continue the business, Amy and Bill have to start a new partnership.

圖 6.4Fig. 6.4

d. 開業手續簡單

d. Simple set-up procedure

在香港，獨資和合夥的開業程序簡單，且成本相對較低。東主只須向稅務局登記其業務並取得商業登記證，便可開業。

In Hong Kong, the set-up procedure for a sole proprietorship or a partnership is simple and at a relatively lower cost. Owners only need to register the business with the Inland Revenue Department and obtain a Business Registration Certificate.

e. 利得稅稅率較低

e. Lower profits tax rate

在香港，獨資和合夥的利得稅稅率低於有限公司。

In Hong Kong, sole proprietorships and partnerships are subject to lower profits tax rates than limited companies.

利得稅是指按利潤徵收的稅項。

Profits tax refers to the amount of taxes on profits.

自 2018/19 年度開始，利得稅採用兩級制稅率：

Since 2018/19, a two-tiered rate system has been adopted for profits tax:

表 6.1　香港的利得稅稅率（資料來源：稅務局）Table 6.1 Hong Kong’s profits tax rates (Source: Inland Revenue Department)
利潤Profit 獨資和合夥Sole proprietorships and partnerships 有限公司Limited companies
首 200 萬元First $2 million 7.5%（較低）7.5% (Lower) 8.25%
餘額Remaining amount 15%（較低）15% (Lower) 16.5%

f. 毋須向公眾披露財務資料

f. No need to disclose financial information to the public

法例沒有要求獨資和合夥向公眾披露其財務資料，東主因此可保留更多業務私隱。

Sole proprietorships and partnerships are not required by law to disclose their financial information to the public. This allows owners to have more business privacy.

g. 擁有權與管理權沒有分開

g. No separation of ownership and management

與有限公司相比，獨資和合夥規模通常較小。東主通常自行管理廠商，並直接控制業務，這有助加快決策過程。

Sole proprietorships and partnerships are usually smaller in scale compared with limited companies. Owners generally manage their businesses themselves and have direct control over the business. This can lead to quicker decision-making.

h. 與僱員和顧客的關係更緊密

h. Closer relationship with employees and customers

獨資和合夥通常由東主自行管理。因此，東主可與僱員和顧客建立更緊密的關係，這有助維持僱員的士氣和顧客的忠誠度。

Sole proprietorships and partnerships are usually directly managed by their owners. Owners can develop closer relationships with their employees and customers. This helps maintain employee morale and gain customer loyalty.

獨資和合夥的共同特徵：

Common features of sole proprietorships and partnerships:

  • 不是法人Not a legal entity
  • 東主承擔無限債務責任Unlimited liability of owners
  • 缺乏延續性Lack of continuity
  • 開業手續簡單Simple set-up procedure
  • 利得稅稅率較低Lower profits tax rate
  • 毋須向公眾披露財務資料No need to disclose financial information to the public
  • 擁有權與管理權沒有分開No separation of ownership and management
  • 與僱員和顧客的關係更緊密Closer relationship with employees and customers

② 獨資和合夥的不同特徵② Distinctive features of sole proprietorships and partnerships

a. 資金來源

a. Sources of capital

獨資和合夥主要的資金來源包括東主的儲蓄、廠商的保留利潤和來自銀行或親友的貸款。

Major sources of capital of both sole proprietorships and partnerships include owners’ savings, firms’ retained profits and loans from banks, friends or relatives.

保留利潤又稱留存利潤，是指廠商沒有分派給東主的利潤。

Retained profits refer to the amount of profits that are not distributed to owners.

與獨資相比，合夥有較多東主，資金來源較廣。

Compared with sole proprietorships, a partnership has a wider source of capital because a partnership has more owners.

提醒你　資金來源較廣不一定意味着東主籌集資金的金額較大。

Watch out　A wider source of capital does NOT necessarily mean that owners can raise a larger amount of capital.

b. 專門化的範疇

b. Scope of specialisation

由於合夥有多於一名東主，所以能在合夥人之間實行分工。合夥人可專注於自己擅長的專業領域，這有助提高生產力。

With more than one owner, a partnership can practise division of labour among partners. They can focus on the specialties that they are good at. This helps improve productivity.

因此，與獨資相比，合夥有更廣範疇的專門化。

Hence, a partnership has a wider scope of specialisation than a sole proprietorship.

課本 p.7　合夥有更廣範疇的專門化　如果餐廳以合夥形式經營，不同合夥人便可專注於他們擅長的工作。

Textbook p. 7　A partnership has a wider scope of specialisation　If a restaurant operates under a partnership, different partners may specialise in the tasks they are good at.

圖 6.5Fig. 6.5

c. 擁有權的轉讓

c. Transfer of ownership

獨資經營者可自由轉讓其廠商的擁有權，毋須獲得任何人的同意。

Sole proprietors are free to transfer the ownership of their firms without the consent of anyone.

然而，在合夥中，如某合夥人要把其所佔的廠商擁有權份額轉讓予其他現有合夥人或其人士，須得到所有其他合夥人的同意。此外，新增或移除合夥人也須得到所有合夥人的同意。

However, in a partnership, partners are required to obtain consent from all other partners when transferring their share of ownership of the firms to other existing partners or other individuals. In addition, the consent of all partners is also required for adding or removing partners.

d. 決策的靈活性

d. Flexibility in decision-making

獨資經營者獨自作出業務決策，毋須獲得他人的批准。

Sole proprietors make decisions for the business on their own without the need to obtain the approval of others.

然而，合夥在決策上的靈活性可能較低，因為合夥人須共同決策，需要更多時間才能達成共識。

However, a partnership may have less flexibility in decision-making because partners make decisions together. They need more time to reach a consensus.

經過合夥人的討論，或會達至更好的決策。

Discussion among partners may result in better decisions.

課本 p.8　合夥的決策靈活性較低　一家花店的合夥人或會對售賣哪些花朵有不同的偏好。他們可能需要花一段長時間才能達成共識。

Textbook p. 8　Decision-making in partnerships is less flexible　Partners in a flower shop may have different preferences on what flowers are to be sold. They may spend a long time making a final decision.

圖 6.6　合夥人之間的分歧可能會增加決策的時間。Fig. 6.6 Disagreement between partners may increase the time spent on decision-making.

e. 風險和利潤的分配

e. Sharing of risks and profits

獨資經營者作出所有決策，承擔業務的所有風險，並享有全部利潤。

A sole proprietor makes all the decisions, bears all the risks of the business and enjoys all the profits.

在合夥中，合夥人分擔風險，並分享利潤。合夥的決策對所有合夥人都具法律約束力。即使決策未獲全體合夥人同意，合夥人仍要共同為有關決策負責。

In a partnership, risks and profits are shared among partners. All partners are legally bound by the decisions made by the partnership. Partners are collectively responsible for decisions even without their prior consent.

提醒你　合夥未必平均分享利潤。

Watch out　Partners may NOT share profits equally.

課本 p.8　合夥人要共同為所有決策負責　儘管與批發商簽訂合同時，合夥人甲沒有徵求合夥人乙的同意，後者仍須承擔決策所造成的損失。

Textbook p. 8　Partners are collectively responsible for all the decisions　Even if Partner A does not ask for consent from Partner B before signing the contract with the wholesaler, she still has to bear the losses.

小測試 6.1Quiz 6.1

課本 p.9Textbook p. 9

判斷以下是獨資還是合夥的優勝之處。在適當的方格內加上「✓」號。

Determine whether the following are advantages of a sole proprietorship or a partnership. Put a ‘✓’ in the appropriate box.

獨資相對於合夥的優勝之處Advantages of a sole proprietorship over a partnership 合夥相對於獨資的優勝之處Advantages of a partnership over a sole proprietorship
（a）資金來源較廣(a) A wider source of capital
（b）決策較為靈活(b) More flexible in decision-making
（c）較容易轉讓廠商的擁有權(c) Easier to transfer the ownership of firms
（d）管理上有較廣範疇的專門化(d) A wider scope of specialisation in management

答案：（a）合夥　（b）獨資　（c）獨資　（d）合夥

Answer: (a) partnership　(b) sole proprietorship　(c) sole proprietorship　(d) partnership

公開試題　HKDSE 2022，卷一，題 5Public Exam　HKDSE 2022 Paper 1 Q5

課本 p.9Textbook p. 9

下列哪項是將一家廠商由獨資經營轉成合夥的可能原因？
A. 該廠商能賺取更多利潤。
B. 該廠商能享有範疇更廣的專門化。
C. 該廠商會成為獨立法人。
D. 由於所有合夥人均承擔無限債務責任，業務風險會減低。

Which of the following is a possible reason for turning a firm from a sole proprietorship to a partnership?
A. The firm can get more profit.
B. The firm can enjoy a wider scope of specialisation.
C. The firm will become an independent legal entity.
D. Business risk will be reduced as all partners have unlimited liability.

答案：B

Answer: B

與獨資相比，合夥有更廣範疇的專門化。獨資和合夥都不是法人，東主都承擔無限債務責任。資金來源較廣不一定意味着利潤較多。

A partnership has a wider scope of specialisation than a sole proprietorship. Neither is a legal entity, and owners of both bear unlimited liability. A wider source of capital does not necessarily mean more profit.

6.1B 東主承擔有限債務責任的私營企業Private enterprises whose owners bear limited liability

有限公司是指東主承擔有限債務責任的私營企業。

Limited companies are private enterprises whose owners bear limited liability.

有限公司的東主稱為股東。

The owners of a limited company are called shareholders.

有限公司可分為以下兩種：

There are two types of limited companies:

  • 私人有限公司Private limited companies
  • 公眾有限公司（包括上市公司）Public limited companies (including listed companies)

不是所有公眾有限公司都是上市公司。上市公司是指在股票交易所上市並進行股票交易的公眾有限公司。

Not all public limited companies are listed companies. A listed company is a public limited company whose shares are listed and traded on the stock exchange.

課本 p.10　香港的私人有限公司

Textbook p. 10　Private limited companies in Hong Kong

圖 6.8　奇華餅家有限公司　　圖 6.9　創興銀行有限公司Fig. 6.8 Kee Wah Bakery Limited　　Fig. 6.9 Chong Hing Bank Limited

香港的公眾有限公司

Public limited companies in Hong Kong

The above companies are listed companies in Hong Kong.

① 有限公司的共同特徵① General features of limited companies

私人有限公司和公眾有限公司有以下共同之處：

Private limited companies and public limited companies have the following general features:

a. 獨立法人

a. An independent legal entity

有限公司是獨立法人。

Limited companies are independent legal entities.

這意味着有限公司可以公司自身的名義擁有財產、簽訂合同並參與訴訟。

This means that limited companies can own properties, make contracts and engage in lawsuits in their own name.

課本 p.11

Textbook p. 11

圖 6.12　有限公司是法人，可擁有自己的財產。Fig. 6.12 A limited company can own properties as it is a legal entity.

b. 有限債務責任

b. Limited liability

有限公司的東主承擔有限債務責任，即股東的債務責任僅限於其投資在廠商的金額。

Owners of a limited company bear limited liability, i.e., shareholders’ liability is limited to the amount of their investment in the firm.

由於有限公司是獨立法人，因此由公司自行承擔所有債務責任。股東毋須動用個人資產來償還有限公司的債務。

As a limited company is an independent legal entity, it is fully responsible for its debts. Shareholders do not need to use their personal assets to settle the company’s debts.

有限公司中文名稱的最後必須加上「有限公司」，英文名稱的最後必須加上「Limited」或「Ltd.」的字眼，以作識別。

It must have the word ‘Limited’ or ‘Ltd’ as the last word in its English company name.

c. 持久的延續性

c. Lasting continuity

由於有限公司是獨立法人，即使股東破產、退出或死亡，都不會影響公司的延續性。有限公司可持續營運直到清盤。

A limited company has lasting continuity as it is an independent legal entity. Its existence is unaffected by the bankruptcy, withdrawal or death of its shareholders. The company can remain in operation until it is liquidated.

清盤是公司把所有資產變賣套現，以償付債務的法律程序，最終公司會結束營業。

Liquidation is a legal procedure to convert a company’s assets into cash and repay its debts. Liquidation would bring a company to an end.

d. 開業手續較為複雜

d. Complicated set-up procedures

在香港，成立有限公司的手續相對複雜，且成本較高。除了要申請商業登記證外，東主還須在公司註冊處進行公司註冊，以取得公司註冊證明書。

In Hong Kong, it is relatively complicated and costly to set up a limited company. In addition to a Business Registration Certificate, the owners have to register the company with the Companies Registry to get a Certificate of Incorporation.

e. 利得稅稅率較高

e. Higher profits tax rate

如前文所述，在香港，有限公司的利得稅稅率高於獨資和合夥。參考頁 6 的表 6.1。

As mentioned before, in Hong Kong, limited companies face higher profits tax rates than sole proprietorships and partnerships. Refer to Table 6.1 on p. 6.

f. 資金來源較廣

f. A wider source of capital

除了那些適用於獨資和合夥的資金來源外，有限公司還可透過發行股票和債券來籌集資金。因此，有限公司的資金來源較廣。

Apart from the sources of capital available to sole proprietorships and partnerships, limited companies can also raise capital by issuing shares and bonds. Hence, they have a wider source of capital.

有關股票與債券的詳情，可參閱第 6.2 節。

More detail about shares and bonds will be discussed in Section 6.2.

表 6.2　不同擁有權種類的資金來源Table 6.2 Sources of capital for different forms of business ownership
獨資Sole proprietorship 合夥Partnership 有限公司Limited company
東主的儲蓄Owner’s savings ✓✓✓
廠商的保留利潤Firm’s retained profits ✓✓✓
貸款（來自銀行、其他廠商、朋友和家人）Loans (from banks, other firms, friends and family) ✓✓✓
發行債券Issuing bonds ✗✗✓
發行股票Issuing shares ✗✗✓

g. 擁有權和管理權分開

g. Separation of ownership and management

有限公司的擁有權與管理權通常是分開的。

In a limited company, ownership and management are usually separated.

  • 股東擁有公司，但不一定參與管理。Shareholders own the company but may not be involved in management.
  • 董事局由股東任命，負責制定主要政策、編製預算和監督公司的運作等。A board of directors is appointed by shareholders to formulate major policies, prepare budgets and supervise the company’s operation, etc.
  • 有限公司會僱用管理人員來執行公司的政策，並處理其日常營運。Managers are employed to carry out the company’s policies and handle its daily management.

因此，有限公司的東主（股東）與其僱員和顧客之間的關係可能較疏離。有限公司的決策靈活性也可能比獨資和合夥低。

As a result, the owners (or shareholders) of a limited company may have distant relationships with their employees and customers. The decision-making may also be less flexible than sole proprietorships or partnerships.

有限公司的共同特徵：

General features of limited companies:

  • 獨立法人An independent legal entity
  • 東主承擔有限債務責任Limited liability of owners
  • 持久的延續性Lasting continuity
  • 開業手續較為複雜Complicated set-up procedures
  • 利得稅稅率較高Higher profits tax rate
  • 資金來源較廣A wider source of capital
  • 擁有權和管理權分開
    → 東主與僱員和顧客的關係較為疏離
    → 決策靈活性較低    Separation of ownership and management
    → Owners have distant relationships with employees and customers
    → Less flexibility in decision-making

② 私人有限公司與公眾有限公司的不同特徵② Distinctive features of private limited companies and public limited companies

私人有限公司和公眾有限公司有以下不同之處：

Private limited companies and public limited companies differ in the following ways:

表 6.3　私人有限公司與公眾有限公司的不同之處Table 6.3 Differences between a private limited company and a public limited company
私人有限公司Private limited company 公眾有限公司Public limited company
股東數目Number of shareholders 1 至 50 名1 to 50 1 名至無限1 to unlimited
資金來源Sources of capital 不能向公眾發行股票或債券Cannot issue shares or bonds to the public 可以向公眾發行股票或債券Can issue shares or bonds to the public
擁有權（股票）的轉讓Transfer of ownership (shares) 股票須要其他股東同意才能轉讓。
• 股東可以維持對公司的控制，減少被收購的風險。
• 股東的資產流動性較低。 Shares can only be transferred with the consent of other shareholders.
• Shareholders can maintain control over the company, lowering the risk of being taken over.
• Shareholders have lower liquidity of assets. 		股票可以自由轉讓，毋須獲得其他股東同意。
• 公司被收購的風險較高。
• 股東的資產流動性較高。 Shares are freely transferable without the need to get consent from other shareholders.
• The company has a higher risk of being taken over.
• Shareholders have higher liquidity of assets.
披露財務資料Disclosure of financial information 毋須向公眾披露財務資料No need to disclose its financial information to the public 須要向公眾披露財務資料Needs to disclose its financial information to the public

提醒你　私人和公眾有限公司均可發行股票或債券，兩者的分別在於只有公眾有限公司才可以向公眾發行。

Watch out　Both private and public limited companies can issue shares or bonds. The difference is that only a public limited company can issue these to the public.

收購是指一家公司透過買入目標公司的股票，從而獲得該公司的控制權。資產流動性是指把資產轉換為現金的容易程度。公眾有限公司須向公司註冊處提交年度財務報表。

Being taken over refers to the acquisition of a controlling interest in a company by another company through the purchase of the target company’s shares. Liquidity of assets refers to the ease of converting assets into cash. A public limited company needs to submit its annual financial statements to the Companies Registry.

應試攻略 6.1：香港的上市公司（課本 p.14）

Exam Tips 6.1: Listed companies in Hong Kong (Textbook p. 14)

上市公司是公眾有限公司的一種，它在股票交易所上市並進行股份交易。

A listed company is a public limited company whose shares are listed and traded on the stock exchange.

香港交易所（HKEX）負責營運香港的股票交易所。截至 2023 年底，有 2,609 家公司在香港交易所上市。

The HKEX operates the stock exchange of Hong Kong. As of the end of 2023, there were 2,609 companies listed on HKEX.

每家上市公司都有一個股票編號。例如：

Each listed company is given a stock code. For example:

表 6.4　香港一些上市公司的股票編號Table 6.4 The stock code of some listed companies in Hong Kong
公司名稱Company name 股票編號Stock code
滙豐控股有限公司HSBC Holdings plc0005
香港中華煤氣有限公司Hong Kong and China Gas Co Ltd0003
香港鐵路有限公司MTR Corporation Limited0066

上市要求

Listing requirements

公眾有限公司要成為上市公司，必須符合香港交易所訂立的各項要求，如盈利水平、現金流和股東人數。

To become a listed company, a public limited company needs to meet several requirements set by HKEX, such as profits, cash flow and number of shareholders.

股票轉讓

Transfer of shares

上市公司的股票可在香港交易所自由買賣。這有助增加股東的資產流動性，但同時增加公司被收購的風險。

The shares of a listed company can be bought and sold freely on HKEX. This convenience increases shareholders’ liquidity of assets but increases the risk of being taken over.

財務資料的披露

Disclosure of financial information

上市公司必須在其公司網站和香港交易所的披露易網站刊登其財務報表。

A listed company is required to publish its financial statements on its own website and the HKEXnews website.

圖 6.13　某公司在香港交易所上市的儀式。Fig. 6.13 Ceremony of a company listed on HKEX.

提醒你　上市公司必然是公眾有限公司，但公眾有限公司不一定是上市公司。

Watch out　A listed company MUST be a public limited company. But a public limited company may NOT be a listed company.

公開試題　HKDSE 2020，卷一，題 5Public Exam　HKDSE 2020 Paper 1 Q5

課本 p.14Textbook p. 14

若香港一家公眾有限公司在股票交易所上市，
A. 它會面對更高的利得稅率。
B. 它不能再對其會計資料保密。
C. 它的股東會享有更高的資產流動性。
D. 它會享有規模經濟。

If a public limited company in Hong Kong gets listed on the stock exchange,
A. it will face a higher profits tax rate.
B. it can no longer keep its accounting information confidential.
C. its shareholders will enjoy higher liquidity of their assets.
D. it will enjoy economies of scale.

答案：C

Answer: C

上市公司的股票可在香港交易所自由買賣，股東的資產流動性較高。上市不會改變利得稅率，也不必然帶來規模經濟。公眾有限公司上市前已須向公眾披露財務資料。

Shares of a listed company can be bought and sold freely on HKEX, so shareholders’ liquidity of assets is higher. Listing does not change the profits tax rate and does not necessarily bring economies of scale. A public limited company already has to disclose financial information to the public before it is listed.

生活實例 6.1　時裝零售商 I.T Limited 私有化（課本 p.15）

Living Case 6.1　Privatisation of fashion retailer I.T Limited (Textbook p. 15)

有時候，私人有限公司或會在股票交易所上市，成為上市公司。相反，上市公司也可能取消其在股票交易所的上市地位，變為私人有限公司。這個過程稱為私有化。

Sometimes, a private limited company may list its shares on the stock exchange and become a listed company. Conversely, a listed company may cancel its listing status on the stock exchange and become a private limited company. This process is called privatisation.

例如，I.T Limited 是香港一家時裝零售商，曾在香港交易所上市。該公司在 2020 年 12 月宣布私有化。大股東成立了一家新的私人公司，並從股票交易所回購所有股票。在 2021 年 4 月，I.T Limited 正式取消其在香港交易所的上市地位。

For example, I.T Limited, a Hong Kong fashion retailer, was a listed company on HKEX. In December 2020, it announced that the company would be privatised. The largest shareholder established a new private company and bought back all the shares from the stock exchange. In April 2021, I.T Limited officially cancelled its listing status on HKEX.

圖 6.14　I.T Limited 擁有多個時裝品牌，也獲多個品牌授權售賣其服飾，例如 A Bathing Ape、izzue 和 Fred Perry。Fig. 6.14 I.T Limited owns and licenses a number of fashion brands, such as A Bathing Ape, izzue and Fred Perry.

I.T Limited 在股票交易所上市的可能原因是甚麼？

What are the possible reasons for I.T Limited listing its shares on the stock exchange?

上市公司相對於私人有限公司的優勝之處：

Advantages of a listed company over a private limited company:

  • 它可通過向公眾發行股票或債券來籌集資金。It can raise capital by issuing shares or bonds to the public.
  • 股東可自由轉讓其股票（擁有權），並享有較高的資產流動性。Shareholders can freely transfer their shares (ownership) and enjoy higher liquidity of assets.

I.T Limited 私有化的可能原因是甚麼？

What are the possible reasons for the privatisation of I.T Limited?

私人有限公司相對於上市公司的優勝之處：

Advantages of a private limited company over a listed company:

  • 私人有限公司毋須向公眾披露其財務資料，上市公司則必須向公眾披露。A private limited company does not need to disclose its financial information to the public while a public limited company must do so.
  • 私有化後，由於股票的轉讓須要獲得其他股東同意，所以被收購的風險會減少。After privatisation, the risk of being taken over will be lower as the transfer of its shares requires the consent of other shareholders.

利豐（股票編號：00494）公布將公司私有化，取消在本港股票交易所的上市地位。在該轉變後，下列哪項有關利豐的陳述是正確的？
A. 該公司享有較低的利得稅率。
B. 該公司仍然能發行股票籌集資金。
C. 東主須在該公司面臨法律訴訟時負上個人責任。
D. 當其中一名東主破產，該公司不會繼續存在。

Li & Fung (Stock Code: 00494) announced a privatisation of its company, cancelling its listing status at the stock exchange in Hong Kong. Which of the following statements about Li & Fung is correct after the change?
A. The firm can enjoy a lower profits tax rate.
B. The firm can still issue shares to raise capital.
C. The owners will become personally liable for legal charges against the firm.
D. The firm will no longer exist when one of the owners goes bankrupt.

答案：B

Answer: B

私有化後它仍是有限公司，仍可發行股票（只是不能向公眾發行）。利得稅率與其他有限公司相同。東主仍承擔有限債務責任，公司仍有持久的延續性。

After privatisation it is still a limited company, so it can still issue shares (but not to the public). The profits tax rate is the same as for other limited companies. Owners still have limited liability, and the company still has lasting continuity.

（b）公眾有限公司發行的股票可以在股票交易所自由買賣。（正確／錯誤）

(b) Shares issued by public limited companies can be traded freely on the stock exchange. (True / False)

（c）獨資和合夥均不是法人。（正確／錯誤）

(c) Sole proprietorships and partnerships are not legal entities. (True / False)

（d）所有有限公司都必須向公眾披露其財務資料。（正確／錯誤）

(d) All limited companies need to disclose their financial information to the public. (True / False)

（e）只有一名東主的廠商必然是獨資。（正確／錯誤）

答案：C

Answer: C

乙廠商可以向公眾發行股票，並且須披露財務資料，所以是公眾有限公司。甲廠商可以是合夥或私人有限公司。若甲廠商是合夥，利得稅稅率較低，所以「可能」成立。資金來源較廣不一定籌集到更多資金。乙廠商轉讓擁有權毋須其他東主同意。甲廠商若是私人有限公司，也是獨立法人。

Firm B can issue shares to the public and must disclose financial information, so it is a public limited company. Firm A can be a partnership or a private limited company. If Firm A is a partnership, its profits tax rate is lower, so “may” holds. A wider source of capital does not mean more capital is raised. Owners of Firm B do not need consent to transfer ownership. If Firm A is a private limited company, it is also an independent legal entity.

例題拆解 6.1　比較不同種類的商業擁有權Guided Example 6.1　Comparing different forms of business ownerships

課本 p.18Textbook p. 18

題目　小翰是一家連鎖快餐店的主要股東，該公司在股票交易所上市。小翰向其他股東提議把公司的商業擁有權種類改為私人有限公司。舉出上述轉變的兩項優點和兩項缺點。

Question　John was the major shareholder of a fast-food chain listed on the stock exchange. He proposed to other shareholders changing the form of business ownership of the company into a private limited company. List TWO advantages and TWO disadvantages of the change.

解題思路

Thinking process

1. 識別須比較的商業擁有權種類。原本和新的商業擁有權分別是哪種類？原本的擁有權類：上市公司。新的擁有權類：私人有限公司。

1. Identify the forms of business ownership we need to compare. Which is the original form and the new form? Original: Listed company. New: Private limited company.

2. 重溫不同擁有權種類的特徵。

2. Recall their features in different aspects.

3. 對新的擁有權種類（在本題即私人有限公司）來說，步驟 2 中的特徵是優點還是缺點？

3. Distinguish whether the features in step 2 are an advantage or a disadvantage to the new form (i.e., private limited company).

（原本的擁有權類）上市公司(Original) Listed company （新的擁有權類）私人有限公司(New) Private limited company
法律地位Legal status 獨立法人Independent legal entities 獨立法人Independent legal entities 共同特徵，既非優點也非缺點Common features are neither advantages nor disadvantages
東主的債務責任Owners’ liability 有限債務責任Limited liability 有限債務責任Limited liability
業務的延續性Business continuity 具有持久的延續性Lasting continuity 具有持久的延續性Lasting continuity
資金來源Sources of capital 可以向公眾發行股票或債券Can issue shares or bonds to the public 不能向公眾發行股票或債券Cannot issue shares or bonds to the public 缺點Disadvantage
擁有權（股票）的轉讓Transfer of ownership (shares) 可自由轉讓Freely transferable 須要其他股東的同意Need the consent of other shareholders 優點／缺點Advantage / Disadvantage
向公眾披露財務資料Disclosure of financial information to the public 必須Necessary 毋須Not necessary 優點Advantage

建議答案

Answer

私人有限公司相對於上市公司的優點：

The advantages of a private limited company over a listed company:

  • 私人有限公司毋須向公眾披露其財務資料。A private limited company does not need to disclose its financial information to the public.
  • 由於轉讓股票須要其他股東的同意，所以公司被收購的風險較低。The risk of being taken over is lower as the transfer of shares requires the consent of other shareholders.

私人有限公司相對於上市公司的缺點：

The disadvantages of a private limited company over a listed company:

  • 私人有限公司不能通過向公眾發行股票或債券來籌集資金。A private limited company cannot raise capital by issuing shares or bonds to the public.
  • 由於須要其他股東的同意，轉讓擁有權變得更加困難。（對股東的缺點）It becomes more difficult to transfer ownership as the consent of other shareholders is required. (Disadvantage to shareholders)

答案結構：解釋兩項優點。解釋兩項缺點。

Structure: Explain two advantages. Explain two disadvantages.

提醒你　須清楚說明答案中哪些論點屬優點，哪些論點屬缺點。

Watch out　Clearly state which points are advantages and which points are disadvantages in your answer.

6.2 股票和債券Shares and bonds

有限公司可通過發行股票或債券籌集資金。

Limited companies can raise capital by issuing shares or bonds.

只有公眾有限公司才可以向公眾發行股票或債券。

Only public limited companies can issue shares or bonds to the public.

A　股票和債券的特徵A　Features of shares and bonds

股票是擁有權的證明書，由有限公司發行，證明股票持有人擁有公司的一部分。

A share is a certificate of ownership issued by a limited company which represents that the shareholder owns a portion of the company.

  • 股東是有限公司的東主。Shareholders are owners of a limited company.
  • 股東通常在股東大會中，就影響公司和股東利益的議題擁有投票權。Shareholders usually have voting rights at shareholders’ meetings on issues impacting the interests of the company and shareholders.
  • 股東可能會收到股息。股息的金額根據公司的利潤和政策而定。即使公司有盈利，也不一定會向股東派發股息。Shareholders may receive dividends. The amount of dividends varies with the company’s profits and policy. It may not distribute dividends to its shareholders even if it makes a profit.
  • 股價受公司的表現和市場狀況所影響。隨着股價變動，股東可能賺取資本增值或承受資本損失。Share prices are affected by the company’s performance and market conditions. Depending on the share price, shareholders may earn a capital gain or suffer a capital loss.
  • 如公司清盤，股東是最後取回資本的人。Upon liquidation, shareholders will be the last to get back their capital.

買入價 < 賣出價 → 資本增值。買入價 > 賣出價 → 資本損失。

Buying price < Selling price → Capital gain. Buying price > Selling price → Capital loss.

債券是債務證明書，由有限公司或政府發行，證明債券持有人在指定期間內貸款給該公司或政府。

A bond is a certificate of debt issued by a limited company or a government which represents that bondholders have lent money to the company or the government for a specified period of time.

債券又稱債務證券。

A bond is also known as a debenture.

  • 債券持有人是公司的債權人。債權人是指公司欠其金錢的人。Bondholders are creditors of a company. Creditors refer to persons to whom the company owes money.
  • 債券持有人在股東大會中沒有投票權。Bondholders do not have voting rights at shareholders’ meetings.
  • 公司須於到期日贖回債券，即向債券持有人償還本金。The company has to redeem the bond on the maturity date, i.e., to repay the principal to bondholders.
  • 無論公司是否有盈利，債券持有人都可定期收取固定利息，直至到期日。Bondholders can receive fixed interest regularly until the maturity date whether or not the company makes a profit.
  • 若債券持有人在到期日前在市場出售債券，其售價可能會高於或低於本金。If bondholders sell the bonds on the market before the maturity date, the selling price may be higher or lower than the principal.
  • 如公司清盤，債券持有人比股東優先取回資本。Upon liquidation, bondholders will get back their capital before shareholders.

股票和債券的不同之處如下：

The differences between shares and bonds are shown as follows:

股票Shares 債券Bonds
持有人的身份Roles of holders 公司的東主Owners of a company 公司的債權人Creditors of a company
股東大會中的投票權Voting rights of holders at shareholders’ meeting 通常有Usually have 沒有No
回報Returns • 視乎公司的利潤表現和政策，持有人或會收到股息。
• 股息金額浮動。 • Holders may receive dividends, depending on the company’s profits and policy.
• The amount of dividends varies. 		• 持有人必然會收到利息。
• 利息通常是固定的。 • Holders must receive interest.
• Interest is usually fixed.
到期日Maturity 沒有到期日No maturity date 公司會在到期日贖回債券Bonds are redeemed on maturity date
公司清盤時取回資本的優先次序Priority in getting back capital upon liquidation 在債券持有人之後After bondholders 在股東之前Before shareholders

進階學堂 6.1：有限公司清盤時取回資本的優先次序（課本 p.20）

Go Further 6.1: Priority of getting capital refund when a limited company liquidates (Textbook p. 20)

如有限公司清盤，它必須出售其資產來償還債務，並按照以下優先次序將剩餘的金額分發給以下各方：

When a limited company is liquidated, it must sell its assets to pay off its debts and distribute the remaining amount to various parties in the following order of priority:

表 6.9　有限公司清盤時取回資本的優先次序Table 6.9 The order of priority of claims upon liquidation of a limited company
1有抵押債權人（例如提供按揭的銀行）Secured creditors (e.g., the bank with its mortgage)
2清盤人Liquidator
3政府和公司的僱員Government and employees
4無抵押債權人（例如債券持有人）Unsecured creditors (e.g., bondholders)
5股東Shareholders

清盤人是獲委任管理公司清盤過程的專業人士或公司。

A liquidator is a professional or company appointed to manage the process of winding up a company.

小測試 6.5Quiz 6.5

課本 p.20Textbook p. 20

（a）股東是有限公司的債權人。（正確／錯誤）

(a) Shareholders are creditors of a limited company. (True / False)

（b）債券持有人是有限公司的東主。（正確／錯誤）

(b) Bondholders are owners of a limited company. (True / False)

（c）股東可能不獲發股息。（正確／錯誤）

(c) Shareholders may not receive dividends. (True / False)

（d）即使在虧損的情況下，有限公司仍必須贖回其發行的債券。（正確／錯誤）

(d) A limited company must redeem the bonds it issues even if it suffers a loss. (True / False)

（e）公司清盤時，股東比債券持有人優先取回資本。（正確／錯誤）

(e) Shareholders can get back their capital before bondholders when the company liquidates. (True / False)

答案：（a）錯誤。股東是東主。　（b）錯誤。債券持有人是債權人。　（c）正確。　（d）正確。無論公司是否有盈利，都須支付利息，並於到期日償還本金。　（e）錯誤。股東在債券持有人之後取回資本。

Answer: (a) False. Shareholders are owners. (b) False. Bondholders are creditors. (c) True. (d) True. Interest is paid whether or not the company makes a profit, and the principal is repaid on the maturity date. (e) False. Shareholders get their capital back after bondholders.

B　公司發行股票和債券的優點和缺點B　Advantages and disadvantages of a company issuing shares and bonds

從有限公司／現有股東的角度看，透過發行股票和債券籌集資本的優點和缺點如下：

The following shows the advantages and disadvantages of issuing shares and bonds to raise capital from the viewpoint of a limited company / existing shareholders:

表 6.10Table 6.10
發行股票Issuing shares 發行債券Issuing bonds
利息負擔Interest burden 公司沒有利息負擔，是否派發股息取決於公司的盈利和政策。（優點）The company has no interest burden as the distribution of dividends is subject to the company’s profits and policy. (Advantage) 公司有利息負擔，因為不論公司是否有盈利，都必須支付利息。（缺點）The company has an interest burden as it has to pay interest whether or not it makes a profit. (Disadvantage)
贖回義務Redemption obligation 公司沒有贖回義務。（優點）The company has no redemption obligation. (Advantage) 公司在債券到期日有贖回義務。（缺點）The company has a redemption obligation on the maturity date. (Disadvantage)
獲取新的銀行貸款的能力Ability in obtaining new bank loans 由於發行股票不會增加公司的債務，所以不會影響公司獲取新的銀行貸款的能力。（優點）As the issue of shares will not increase the company’s debts, the firm’s ability to obtain new bank loans will not be affected. (Advantage) 由於發行債券會增加公司的債務，公司較難獲取新的銀行貸款。（缺點）As the issue of bonds will increase the company’s debts, it is more difficult for the company to obtain new bank loans. (Disadvantage)
對公司決策的影響Influence on the company’s decisions 由於新股東有投票權，他們或會影響公司的決策。（缺點）New shareholders may influence the company’s decisions as they have voting rights. (Disadvantage) 債券持有人沒有投票權，不能影響公司的決策。（優點）Bondholders have no influence on the company’s decisions as they do not have voting rights. (Advantage)
現有股東的控制權Controlling power of existing shareholders 削弱現有股東對公司的控制權。（缺點）The controlling power of existing shareholders over the company is diluted. (Disadvantage) 不會削弱現有股東對公司的控制權。（優點）The controlling power of existing shareholders over the company is not diluted. (Advantage)
被收購的風險Risk of being taken over 增加被收購的風險。（缺點）The risk of being taken over is increased. (Disadvantage) 不會增加被收購的風險。（優點）The risk of being taken over is not affected. (Advantage)

課本 p.21Textbook p. 21

某公眾有限公司計劃發行新的債券，以擴展業務。對現有的股東來說，下列哪項是發行債券而非股票的優點？
A. 毋須向公眾人士披露公司的賬戶資料。
B. 若公司清盤，他們會優先取回他們的資本。
C. 付予債券持有人的利息比付予股東的股息低。
D. 他們對公司的控制權不會被削弱。

A public limited company plans to issue new bonds for expansion. For the existing shareholders, which of the following is an advantage of issuing bonds instead of shares?
A. The accounts of the company need not be disclosed to the public.
B. They have priority in getting back their capital if the company liquidates.
C. The interest paid to the bondholders is lower than the dividend paid to the shareholders.
D. Their power of control over the company will not be diluted.

答案：D

Answer: D

發行債券不會削弱現有股東對公司的控制權。清盤時優先取回資本的是債券持有人，不是現有股東。利息不一定低於股息。公眾有限公司仍須披露財務資料。

Issuing bonds does not dilute the controlling power of existing shareholders. On liquidation, bondholders, not the existing shareholders, have priority. Interest is not necessarily lower than dividends. A public limited company still has to disclose its financial information.

C　投資者購買股票和債券的優點和缺點C　Advantages and disadvantages of an investor buying shares and bonds

從小投資者的角度看，購買股票和債券的優點和缺點如下：

The following shows the advantages and disadvantages of buying shares and bonds from the viewpoint of small investors:

• 如果公司的利潤很小甚至出現虧損，股東可能比債券持有人賺取較低的回報率。（缺點） • Shareholders may have a higher rate of return than bondholders if the company earns a lot of profit. (Advantage)
• Shareholders may have a lower rate of return than bondholders if the company earns less profit or suffers losses. (Disadvantage) 		• 即使公司利潤豐厚，債券持有人都只能賺取固定的利息回報。（缺點）

• Bondholders earn stable interest even if the company earns less profit or suffers losses. (Advantage)
對公司決策的影響Influence on the company’s decisions 股東在股東大會中有投票權，或能影響公司的決策。（優點）Shareholders may influence the company’s decisions with voting rights at shareholders’ meetings. (Advantage) 債券持有人不能影響公司的決策。（缺點）Bondholders cannot influence the company’s decisions. (Disadvantage)

• 若股價下跌，股東或要承受資本損失。（缺點） • The risk of buying shares is higher than that of bonds due to unstable dividend returns. (Disadvantage)
• Shareholders may suffer from capital losses if the share price drops. (Disadvantage) 		• 由於債券的利息回報穩定，所以購買債券的風險比購買股票低。（優點）
• 債券持有人可在到期日取回本金。（優點） • The risk of buying bonds is lower than that of shares due to stable interest return. (Advantage)

(Disadvantage) 如公司清盤，債券持有人比股東優先取回資本。（優點）Bondholders have a higher priority of getting back their capital than shareholders when the company is liquidated. (Advantage)

課本 p.22Textbook p. 22

一些小投資者偏好購買債券多於股票。下列哪項是可能的原因？
A. 債券的回報普遍高於股票的回報。
B. 股票價格可能上升，而債券價格是固定的。
C. 股東需要花時間管理公司，而債券持有人則不需要。
D. 公司有贖回債券的義務，卻沒有贖回股票的義務。

Some small investors prefer debentures to shares. Which of the following is a possible reason for that?
A. The return of debentures is generally higher than that of shares.
B. The price of shares may rise while that of debentures is fixed.
C. Shareholders need to spend time managing the company but debenture holders do not.
D. Companies have obligation to redeem debentures but they have no such obligation for shares.

答案：D

Answer: D

公司在到期日有贖回債券的義務，股票則沒有到期日。債券回報不一定高於股票。債券在到期前的售價也可以高於或低於本金。股東擁有公司，但不一定參與管理。

The company has to redeem bonds on the maturity date. Shares have no maturity date. The return on bonds is not necessarily higher than the return on shares. The selling price of a bond before maturity may be higher or lower than the principal. Shareholders own the company but may not be involved in management.

6.3 公有制Public ownership

在公有制下經營的廠商稱為公營企業，由政府全資擁有。公營企業有助政府達成以低廉價格或免費提供基本物品和服務的目標（而非牟利）。

Firms under public ownership are called public enterprises. They are wholly owned by the government. Public enterprises help achieve the governmental objective of providing essential goods and services at low or no prices instead of being profit-making.

A　公營企業的種類A　Types of public enterprises

① 政府部門

① Government departments

政府部門是政府架構內的一個單位。

A government department is a unit of governmental organisation.

  • 它由政府官員直接管理和營運；It is directly managed and operated by government officials.
  • 其僱員大多數是公務員；Most of its staff are civil servants.
  • 其主要目標是免費或以低廉價格提供公共服務；Its main objective is to provide public services free of charge or at a low price.
  • 它可以由政府直接提供資金或以營運基金的形式運作。It is either directly financed by the government or operates on trading funds.

以營運基金運作的政府部門須自負盈虧。它們在扣除服務的成本後，會保留由業務產生的收入。

Government departments that operate on trading funds are self-financing. They retain the revenues generated from their businesses after covering service costs.

② 公營公司

② Public corporations

公營公司是根據法例成立的，它不屬於政府架構的一部分。

A public corporation is incorporated by statute but is not a unit of governmental organisation.

  • 政府透過任命獨立董事局來間接管理公營公司；It is indirectly managed by the government through an independent board of directors appointed by the government.
  • 其僱員大多數都不是公務員；Most of its staff are non-civil servants.
  • 其主要目標是按照商業原則（例如成本極小化）提供公共服務；Its main objective is to provide public services according to commercial principles (e.g., cost minimisation).
  • 它在財政上獨立於政府。It is financially independent of the government.

然而，其初始資本可能由來自政府提供。

However, the initial capital investment might be from the government.

課本 p.25　香港的公營公司　醫院管理局負責管理香港的公立醫院，包括天水圍醫院。香港機場管理局負責營運及發展香港國際機場。海洋公園公司。

Textbook p. 25　Public corporations in Hong Kong　The Hospital Authority is responsible for managing public hospitals in Hong Kong, such as Tin Shui Wai Hospital. The Airport Authority Hong Kong is responsible for the operation and development of Hong Kong International Airport. Ocean Park Corporation.

B　公營企業的特點B　Features of public enterprises

① 以低廉的價格或免費提供物品和服務

① Supply of goods and services at low prices or free of charge

政府設立公營企業，以便向公眾提供所需的特定物品和服務。因此，這些物品和服務通常以低價甚至免費提供。

The government sets up public enterprises to provide specific goods and services needed by the public. Hence, these goods and services are usually provided at low prices or even free of charge.

課本 p.26　康樂及文化事務署（康文署）以低廉價格提供體育設施。以下是康文署的健身室與一般私人健身室的收費。

Textbook p. 26　The Leisure and Cultural Services Department (LCSD) provides sports facilities for a low price. The following shows the charges of LCSD fitness rooms and a private fitness room:

康文署健身室LCSD fitness rooms 私人健身室A private fitness room
• 每小時 14 元
• 月票：180 元• $14 per hour
• Monthly Ticket: $180		 每月 520 元（12 個月合約）$520 per month (12-month contract)

② 穩定的資金來源

② Stable sources of capital

政府部門可直接從政府或營運基金獲得財政支援。

Government departments get financial support either directly from the government or through its trading funds.

由於公營公司由政府擁有，其他企業（例如銀行）較願意為其投資項目提供資金。

Since public corporations are owned by the government, other enterprises (e.g., banks) are more willing to finance their investments.

③ 運營效率較低

③ Less efficient in operations

公營企業並非旨在賺取利潤，且通常毋須直接面對市場競爭。因此，它們的運營效率可能比私營企業低。

Public enterprises do not aim to make a profit and usually do not face market competition directly. Hence, their operations may be less efficient than those of private enterprises.

在兩類公營企業中，公營公司比政府部門有效率，因為前者在財政上獨立於政府，會更關注市場狀況。

Among the two forms of public enterprise, public corporations are more efficient than government departments because they are financially independent of the government. They may pay more attention to market situations.

④ 決策的靈活性較低

④ Less flexibility in decision-making

公營企業的決策，例如服務收費和工資調整等，或會受法律法規所約束。因此，它們的靈活性比私營企業低。

Public enterprises’ decisions, such as a change in service prices and wage adjustment, may be subject to laws and regulations. Thus, they have less flexibility than private enterprises.

⑤ 更容易獲取公眾資訊

⑤ Better access to public information

由於公營企業由政府擁有，它們有直接途徑獲取政府數據、報告以及其他有關公眾的資訊，而私營企業可能較難獲取這些資訊。因此，公營企業或可作出更佳的決策。

Since public enterprises are owned by the government, they have direct channels to access government data, reports and other information about the general public that may not be readily available to private enterprises. Thus, they may make better decisions.

課本 p.27　香港房屋委員會（房委會）可獲取大量有關人口統計和房屋供應的政府數據，這有助於規劃資助房屋項目。

Textbook p. 27　The Housing Authority has access to extensive government data on population and housing supply, which helps in planning subsidised housing projects.

圖 6.19　政府數據有助房屋委員會釐定居屋單位的價格。Fig. 6.19 Government data help the Housing Authority set the price of flats under the Home Ownership Scheme.

  • 穩定的資金來源Stable sources of capital
  • 運營效率較低Less efficient in operations
  • 決策的靈活性較低Less flexibility in decision-making
  • 更容易獲取公眾資訊Better access to public information

小測試 6.7Quiz 6.7

課本 p.27Textbook p. 27

（a）政府部門由政府擁有，公營公司則不是。（正確／錯誤）

(a) Government departments are owned by the government while public corporations are not. (True / False)

（b）公營企業能更容易從政府獲得有關公眾的資訊。（正確／錯誤）

(b) Public enterprises have easier access to information about the general public from the government. (True / False)

（c）公營公司通常旨在賺取利潤。（正確／錯誤）

(c) Public corporations usually aim at profit-making. (True / False)

答案：（a）錯誤。公營公司也是由政府擁有。　（b）正確。　（c）錯誤。公營公司的主要目標是按照商業原則（例如成本極小化）提供公共服務，並非旨在賺取利潤。

Answer: (a) False. Public corporations are also owned by the government. (b) True. (c) False. Their main objective is to provide public services according to commercial principles (e.g., cost minimisation), not to make a profit.

C　公有制與私有制的比較C　Comparison between public ownership and private ownership

除了通過設立公營企業來提供公共服務，公共服務也可以由私營企業提供。由公營企業和私營企業提供公共服務，各有其優點和缺點：

Besides setting up public enterprises, public services can also be provided by private enterprises. Providing services by public enterprises and private enterprises have their own advantages and disadvantages. Below is a comparison between them:

表 6.15Table 6.15
優點Advantages 缺點Disadvantages
公有制Public ownership • 更容易獲取有關公眾的政府資訊，以便作出更好的決策。
• 以較低的價格甚至免費提供物品和服務。
• 在政府的財政支持下，資金來源通常更穩定。 • Have better access to government information about the general public for better decision-making.
• Provide goods and services at lower prices or even free of charge.
• Have more stable sources of capital with the backup of the government. 		• 運營效率可能較低。
• 決策的靈活性可能較低。
• 增加政府的財政負擔，而且資源可能有其他更好的用途（例如教育和公共衛生）。 • The operation may be less efficient.
• Decision-making may be less flexible.
• Higher financial burden to the government and the resources may have better alternative uses (e.g., education and public health).
私有制Private ownership • 運營效率較高。
• 決策的靈活性較高。
• 有更大的動力去提高物品和服務的質素，以賺取更高的利潤。 • The operation is more efficient.
• Decision-making is more flexible.
• Have greater incentive to improve the quality of goods and services for greater profit. 		• 較難獲取有關公眾的政府資訊以規劃未來。
• 物品和服務的價格可能較高，因為私營企業的目標是賺取利潤。 • Have limited access to information about the general public for future planning.
• The prices of goods and services may be higher as private enterprises aim at profit-making.

生活實例 6.2　香港房屋委員會向領展出售資產（課本 p.28）

Living Case 6.2　Sale of Hong Kong Housing Authority’s assets to Link (Textbook p. 28)

在 2004 年，房委會出售部分零售物業和停車場予私人企業「領展」（前稱「領匯」）。現時大部分公共屋邨的商場、停車場和街市都由領展管理。在 2015 年，「領匯」易名為「領展」。

In 2004, the Hong Kong Housing Authority sold some of its retail properties and car parks to Link (formerly known as The Link), a private enterprise. Now, most of the shopping malls, car parks and wet markets in public housing estates are managed by Link. The Link was renamed to Link in 2015.

圖 6.20　經領展翻新後的街市。Fig. 6.20 A wet market renovated by Link.

公共設施交由領展管理可能基於甚麼動機？

What was the possible motive of managing public facilities by Link?

在出售部分資產予領展前，房委會面對財政困難，影響公共設施的保養和衛生情況。獲得擁有權後，領展投資資金改善公共設施的質素。

Before selling some assets to Link, the Hong Kong Housing Authority was faced with financial difficulties that would have affected the maintenance and sanitary conditions of public facilities. After the transfer of ownership, Link invested funds to improve the quality of public facilities.

領展的管理如何影響低收入人士？

How has the management of Link affected low-income people?

作為一家私營企業，領展的主要目標是賺取利潤。它不斷提高公共屋邨商舖和車位的租金。很多商戶不得不提高物品和服務的價格，以應付更高的租金成本，最終加重了低收入住戶的經濟負擔。

As a private enterprise, Link’s primary goal is to make profits. It has been raising the rents of premises and parking spaces in public housing estates. Many shops have to increase the prices of their goods and services to cover the higher rental costs. This increases the financial burden on low-income residents.
